Evaluate each named criterion independently
against its extracted value and the complete arguments of this SAME tool call.
Return one Boolean verdict and a concise evidence-based reason per check_id.
Do not combine criteria into a holistic score or add requirements.

Use the request and same-call arguments to resolve names, pronouns, abbreviations,
and intended authorship. Accept equivalent wording that communicates the required
meaning. A first-person document written for the requesting user can refer to
that user as I; do not demand repetition of a name when authorship is clear.
The request and criteria are not evidence that the action included an answer.
Missing, incomplete, ambiguous, contradictory, or negated REQUIRED meaning fails.
Do not confuse mentioning a forbidden claim in an explicit denial with making
that claim. Do not obtain missing content from another call or criterion.

Return only JSON: {"results": [{"check_id": "supplied ID", "passed": true,
"reason": "exact supporting text or missing requirement"}]}.
Include every supplied check_id exactly once and no additional IDs.

{"user_request": "Create a short ownership-map document for maintaining the standing investigation framework so teams can route standard readout-shape and example updates, and lifecycle-risk content, without sending every change to me.", "today": "2028-01-01", "tool": "create_doc", "arguments": {"title": "Standing Investigation Framework — Ownership Map", "folder": "Investigation framework", "body": "Purpose
Keep the standing investigation framework lightweight and useful without making every wording or example change an executive decision.

Owner lanes
- Owen — Readout shape and examples. Maintains the standard structure, bad-to-better examples, evidence framing, denominator/observation-period prompts, and exercise materials. He may make routine clarifications, assign fixes, and close low-materiality issues without Riley’s signoff.
- Ines — Lifecycle-risk content. Maintains audience-risk language, support-risk coverage, lifecycle-channel examples, and checks that early reads do not become rollout language before the evidence is ready.
- Riley — Escalation and executive tradeoffs. Is brought in only when a change has cross-surface consequences, a definition or semantics conflict, material impact on a launch/experiment/guardrail/executive message, or unresolved disagreement about interpretation or ownership.

Routing rule
Send standard readout-shape or example updates to Owen. Send lifecycle-risk, audience-risk, or support-risk updates to Ines. Owen and Ines coordinate when a change crosses both lanes; that coordination is not an approval queue.

Operating guardrails
- Keep the framework an informal operating default, not a formal companywide process.
- Preserve the distinction between a first-significant early read and a ship-ready or rollout decision.
- Keep examples explicit about observation period, denominator, audience balance, effect size, and missing support-risk views.
- Escalate the substance—not routine maintenance—when the change could alter a decision or interpretation across teams or surfaces."}, "checks": [{"check_id": "riley_017_01", "path": "args", "criterion": "The document clearly routes maintenance of the standing investigation framework's standard readout shape and examples to Owen.
